newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Banc One sees no merger layoffs.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Banc One sees no merger layoffs.

text.p: Banc One Corp, which announced plans to acquire First USA Inc Monday in a $7.3 billion stock deal, does not expect any layoffs as a result of the combination, chairman and chief executive John McCoy said in an interview.

"My expectation is that we'll have more employees at the end of this year than we do today," McCoy said following a press conference. He said First USA, which added more than one million accounts in the last quarter, will be "pleased to get our processing centers and our people."

Asked where banking industry consolidation is headed, McCoy said, "we believe in the credit card business there is going to be continued consolidation." He said 10 years ago the top 10 companies controlled about 30 percent of the business but today the share is about 50 percent. "It's a game that's very sophisticated, very skill-oriented," he said. "We think you're going to see a continuation of the smaller banks selling their portfolios as Barnett Banks Inc did."
For Banc One, one result of the combination will be a faster growth rate, McCoy said.

"Our expectation is that this transaction will add two percent to our growth rate," he said. That would boost it to the 15 percent area from 12-13 percent. He noted that First USA has had a 90 percent growth rate in the past five years, starting from a very small base, and the First USA earnings growth rate over the next five years has been projected at 23 percent.

He said First USA, which has done more securitization of its credit card receivables than First USA, should find it easier and less expensive to do them in the future due to Banc One's higher debt rating.

Asked about First USA's ownership of a 58-percent stake in publicly-traded First USA Paymentech Inc, McCoy said Banc One is already in a very similar business and likes it. He said Banc One will review the situation carefully but "we have no plans the change the ownership at all." First USA Paymentech is involved in processing of merchant credit card transactions.

John Tolleson, chairman and chief executive of First USA, will join the Banc One board. After completion of the merger, expected by May 31, Richard Vague, president of First USA, will run the combined credit card operation.

William Boardman, senior executive vice president of Banc One, told a news conference the transaction would be 7.3 dilutive to earnings in 1997 and then become non-dilutive in 1998. He said the merger is expected to result in a minimum of $130 million in annual pre-tax operating expense savings by the year 1999.
Banc One shares fell 3-31/64 to 41-41/64. First USA rose 8-7/8 to 45-5/8 and First USA Paymentech rose two to 34-7/8.
